findings.gate: Reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence) / charter §4.3 (costs ledgered forward)

draft_evidence.quote: Karis's hand. The bound one, the cut across the palm from a stave's edge in a cut, twelve days old, bound by Brom with thread and a strip of shirt and his teeth

comparison_evidence.quote: Karis: a cut, on the back of the left hand, shallow, from the stone — she had gone down against the wall when the boxes went down and had put her hand on a step's edge and the edge had been a step's edge

findings.consequence: Three facts about a wound the reader watched happen six chapters ago are restated wrongly in one clause: the site (palm, not the back of the hand), the cause (a stave's edge, i.e. an enemy weapon, rather than a step's edge she fell against) and the age (twelve days; ch12.md line 129 dates it 'Two hundred and ninetieth day' and this chapter's dawn is the 299th, so eight days). The cause error is the costly one — it converts Karis, whose whole beat at the reach was that she went down against a wall and did not fight, into someone struck by a weapon, and it contradicts the arithmetic the book has been keeping openly. The age error then repeats at line 73 ('who had been writing with it for twelve days'), so the mistake carries a beat with it.
findings.repair_target: ch18.md lines 65 and 73 — restate as the back of the left hand, cut on a step's edge, eight days old; adjust line 73's 'twelve days' to match. Oryn's 'Don't write with it for a week' can stand either way but reads more precisely against a hand-back cut.

draft_evidence.quote: and because she had come two days out of her route for it and was going to have it whole.

findings.category: continuity — unpaid promise at the scene of the promise

draft_evidence.quote: She did the line. Five, then four, then the small ones, in the register, one hand each for the small ones and the current for none of them, because none needed it and she did not have it to spend

comparison_evidence.quote: It'll hold to the spring. In the spring I'll do it again. Don't go up the ladder.

findings.consequence: Oryn made a dated promise at this exact ford, to a named-by-role patient, for this exact season: in the spring she would do the knee again. A reader who remembers B7 ch18 sees the healer keep an absent appointment and skip the present one, which is precisely the opposite of the chapter's argument about her. draft_evidence.quote: But he heard Cleon, in the door with the key: *If that fragment ever reads something for you that shouldn't be made and reads it anyway.

comparison_evidence.quote: He had stood in the door with the key in his hand and the lamp behind him and the dark of the quarry behind the lamp, and had not come out onto the step, because the step was the street's.

findings.gate: Voice charter §8.2 (a sentence must land identically read aloud)

draft_evidence.quote: *If that fragment ever reads something for you that shouldn't be made and reads it anyway. Don't tell me. Don't tell anyone. Just remember I said it.*

comparison_evidence.quote: If that fragment ever reads something for you that shouldn't be *made* and reads it anyway — " He stopped. "Don't tell me. Don't tell anyone. Just remember I said it.

findings.consequence: In Ch13 the conditional is deliberately unfinished — the dash and 'He stopped' are the beat: a careful man refusing to say the apodosis. Recalled here with a full stop, it becomes a headless conditional presented as a complete sentence, which reads as a typo on the page and, in narration, will be voiced as a flat declarative that has lost the refusal. The italic on '*made*' is also dropped, which is harmless inside a fully italicised recall.
findings.repair_target: ch18.md line 123 — restore the trailing dash so the recalled line stops where Cleon stopped it.

findings.gate: Voice charter §9 (anti-tic; a repeated beat phrase is a defect) / shared voice: 'Explaining subtext after the dialogue already conveyed it'

draft_evidence.quote:
"Noted," Vastin said, and she looked at him. "That's new."

"It's a useful word."

"It's his."

comparison_evidence.quote: "It's a good word," she said, and went out to the bank to see about the mule.

findings.consequence: 'Noted' appears six times in the chapter and is remarked on four times in seventy-five lines ('That's new.' / 'It's a useful word.' / 'It's his.' / 'It's a good word.'). The first exchange is a genuine beat — Vastin taking Cael's word is real character movement and it earns its moment. The repetitions afterward turn the series' signature into a thing the book is admiring about itself, which is the one register this narrator does not use. Cutting the last one costs nothing and lets the first land harder.
findings.repair_target: ch18.md line 159 — replace or drop 'It's a good word,' keeping the exchange at lines 83-87 intact.

concerns: Causal-conjunction density. 'because' appears 52 times in 4,911 words (10.6 per thousand). Measured against the recent chapters by the same hand: ch13 9.2, ch16 8.1, ch17 8.4, ch15 7.9. This is the highest in the run and roughly 26% above the previous high. The construction is house voice and should not be sanded away, but at this density the sentence scaffold starts to announce itself, which is the shared-voice failure mode 'repeated sentence scaffolds that make scenes feel generated'. Taste, not contract — logged here, not as a finding.

The leaf offer discloses a little more than 'offered and declined'. Lira's 'It's a leaf. Older than the board. It says what the thing was built for' (line 153) hands Oryn the leaf's existence, its age relative to the board, and its subject before she declines. She is not told what it says or that it is about Cael's kind, so the prohibited outcome ('No leaf told to Oryn') is not breached; but the offer sits at the outer edge of what an offer needs, and Ch21 will be reading back what Oryn did and did not know at this ford.

Oryn gives 'a man on this bank with ribs I've been owed a reading of since a marsh' (line 39) as a reason to walk east beyond the two days her own holds account for — but she does the reading that same evening, so the reason is spent by nightfall and the chapter never replaces it. The other reason she gives (two Quiet places and what they cost) carries the weight fine; the ribs clause just does not survive the night.

The standing order is not weighed in the withholding ledger. B7 ch24 closes on 'a still place at the middle of them that he had read three times and had not touched since, because a healer had said *stop* and he had stopped'. In this chapter the twelfth reads that place while Oryn's hands are on him. Line 143 is an honest, well-built accounting of why he does not tell her — but the strongest item against him is missing from it: the thing he has just done is the thing she told him to stop doing. The draft covers it obliquely ('it was the only time in the reading that he was not lying still', line 113) and does establish that he did not choose it, so this is a craft opportunity rather than a proven defect.

Lira is 'always first' (ch13.md line 61: 'because Lira was always first, and had been since a hall'). Withholding the Rune finding from everyone breaks a four-year pattern, and the chapter's ledger of reasons (line 143) addresses only Oryn. Ch22 will presumably pay this; noting it here so the repair pass does not close the door.

Seven-holds geography, for planning rather than for the author: B7 ch18 has Millrace as the third of Oryn's seven ('I'm at the third, and the fourth is four days on'), while ch17.md and this packet's knowledge_boundary put all seven north of Millrace. Line 39 follows ch17 and the packet, which is the right call at this seat, but the two accounts cannot both stand and Ch21/Ch24 will lean on her circuit.

Packet hygiene, for the orchestrator rather than the author: the compiled packet's copy of the previous chapter (ch17) is STALE. It still carries 'six and a mule' and Teague's older 'you six less your researcher, who doesn't fight' line, both of which the on-disk ch17.md has since been repaired away from (DECISIONS rows 16 and 24). The author appears to have drafted the mule against the ruling rather than against the packet, which was the right call and is why the mule reads correctly — but the same staleness is the likeliest source of the two-non-fighters wording in the closing image (F-008), and the packet's knowledge_boundary line 'five days to the Span ... past the fourth' is the likeliest source of F-003. Recompiling ch17 and correcting that knowledge_boundary line before the r2 packet would remove two of the ten findings at source.
strengths: The fixed line lands verbatim and lands in the right place — after the reading, in the near dark, with her looking at him and not at the ford (line 133), so the register-break carries the certainty rather than the words having to.

The deep reading is dramatized from inside the patient, which is the hardest possible angle and the only one available: 'Her current ... ran down through the twelve to the middle, to the place, and did not arrive. It went round' (line 105), and then the river/stone image at the end of it, which explains the still place without theorizing it. This is the chapter and it works.

Oryn's terms are restated at their full length without becoming a speech about herself: the arithmetic is concrete (seven holds, four walked, three owed), the concession is bounded (two days on her way, further for stated reasons), and the refusal is aimed past the six at the one man on the road who has not heard it (line 39). Her independent want is intact and costed — charter §7.4 satisfied for the book.

The two healers price each other in a single exchange with no dialogue and the narration closes the file on it: 'that was the whole of the exchange between the two healers on the bearing, then or after, and Cael entered it as complete' (line 21). Restraint doing the work.

Vastin taking an order from a woman at a plank table and standing there (line 29), then using Cael's word (line 83), is the chapter's quietest and best progression beat — human-track movement with no number attached.

The mule ruling is executed cleanly and invisibly: the crew comes down with no mule, the mule is hers and already at the ford, and Oryn loads Karis's boxes onto it herself without comment (lines 5, 159, 171). A repair that reads as if it had always been the plan.

The withholding is reasoned on the page in the character's own accounting register (line 143) — Cleon's warning, the absence of words, and the refusal to lay a rival instrument's reading over a healer's finding on her own bench. It keeps the two instruments' disagreement live without letting Cael off the hook, and it is the strongest single paragraph in the chapter.

Tic discipline and the reader standard are clean on measurement: one one-word paragraph, zero capped phrases, zero forbidden names, zero banned-register words, and a closer that differs in kind from Ch17's log.
